sources.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
sources.evidence: Dated August 20, 2019. Explicitly announces the public 774M GPT-2 release after the February small and May medium releases. Distinguishes the newly released 774M model from the still unreleased largest model and earlier partner research. Reopened October 27: the first paragraph directly calls this the 774 million parameter model; no separate active-parameter count is stated.

sources.title: Original 774M release commit
sources.evidence: The August 20, 2019 commit adds the 774M checkpoint to download instructions and Docker builds. Its README corrects earlier erroneous parameter labels and identifies the large 774M version as released. The README at this exact commit was fetched again on October 27 and explicitly lists large (774M parameter), with the footnote correcting erroneous earlier counts.

sources.title: GPT-2 model card, November 2019
sources.evidence: Identifies OpenAI as developer, lists the released 774M variant, and describes WebText-trained generative text models. Its February model date is not the public release date of this checkpoint. Reopened the complete original card on October 27; it names the 774 million parameter model but gives no activated-parameter convention.

sources.title: Original 774M checkpoint hyperparameters
sources.evidence: Exact checkpoint configuration specifies 50,257 vocabulary entries, 1,024 context positions, 36 blocks, hidden width 1,280 and 20 attention heads. Fresh HTTP 200 retrieval on October 27 reconfirmed all five values.

sources.title: Original GPT-2 model implementation
sources.evidence: Complete implementation constructs dense causal attention and biasful fourfold MLPs, two learned norms per block, final learned norm, learned token and position embeddings. Output logits reuse token embeddings; causal masks and key/value caches are computed rather than learned checkpoint variables. Fresh October 27 reading independently reconfirmed the learned-parameter formula, yielding 774,030,080 from the original 774M hyperparameters; no checkpoint data or new tensor census was used in this pass.

sources.title: Original 774M TensorFlow checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Read the complete 15,535-byte original index and reconstructed all 436 variable names and shapes from exact hyperparameters and original module code. All variables are F32 learned parameters, totaling 774,030,080. No optimizer slots, buffers, packed values or scales are present. Contiguous storage offsets end at 3,096,120,320 bytes, matching a HEAD-only request for the data file. No weight data were downloaded.

sources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
sources.evidence: Section 2.3 and Table 2 describe the 36-layer, width-1280 Transformer under its earlier erroneous 762M label, with a 50,257-token vocabulary and 1,024-token context. The report describes WebText training and text completion. Commonsense reasoning benchmarks do not establish a dedicated reasoning mode. Rechecked Section 2.3 and Table 2 against the full PDF fetched October 27; these are architecture/total-size specifications, not an active-parameter table.

sources.title: Current original-repository Modified MIT License
sources.evidence: Current official code-and-model repository labels the terms Modified MIT, including added generated-content language. This is the currently published license label, not the license present at the August 2019 release.

sources.title: License at the August 2019 public release
sources.evidence: The license at the exact 774M release commit is plain MIT. This historical text is preserved separately from the later Modified MIT terms.

sources.title: January 2020 license update
sources.evidence: The January 3, 2020 commit changes MIT to Modified MIT and adds generated-content terms. A January 4 cleanup follows. This confirms that the modified terms postdate this model release; no legal conclusion about earlier grants is inferred.

sources.title: Original GPT-2 announcement and May interim update
sources.evidence: The February announcement releases only a smaller checkpoint. The May update describes sharing the then-labelled 762M model with selected research partners, not a general public weight release.

sources.title: Bigram Subnetworks: Mapping to Next Tokens in Transformer Language Models
sources.publisher: Tyler A. Chang and Benjamin K. Bergen, UC San Diego
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 inspection of Section 3.1 and Figure 1: GPT-2 large is the original 774M model, but the active-parameter figures measure learned binary masks over frozen model parameters for sparse bigram subnetworks. The masks exclude embeddings and layer norms. These are modified-subnetwork counts, not a published active count for the complete released GPT-2 large checkpoint.

sources.title: Small Batch Size Training for Language Models: When Vanilla SGD Works, and Why Gradient Accumulation Is Wasteful
sources.publisher: Martin Marek et al., New York University and Columbia University
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 inspection of Appendix A.1 and Table 1: the explicit active count concerns a newly trained GPT-2-labelled 124M experiment, with 162M total parameters, untied embeddings, RMSNorm, RoPE, QK-norm and changed head dimensions. Neither checkpoint identity nor architecture matches the original GPT-2 large; its active-count convention cannot establish this model's value.

name.note: Retain the corrected official 774M size label for identity; the exact count is recorded separately.

developer.note: The original announcement, model card and report identify OpenAI.

family.note: This is the large GPT-2 checkpoint, released before the largest 1.5B version.

release_date.note: The dated announcement and release commit agree on general public availability. Earlier paper publication and selected-partner access do not establish a public release.

open_weights.note: The release explicitly distributes weights. Its original public metadata and data-file HEAD request were accessible during this audit.

license.note: Current official repository terms are Modified MIT. The August 2019 release originally carried plain MIT; the modified text was introduced in January 2020. This records published terms and their history without inferring revocation of earlier grants.

parameters_b.note: Retain 774,030,080 learned parameters, corroborated on October 27 by the original configuration and implementation: 50,257×1,280 + 1,024×1,280 + 36×(12×1,280² + 13×1,280) + 2×1,280. Tied input/output embeddings count once. The prior complete checkpoint-index census remains supporting evidence; this pass did not repeat it or download weights. OpenAI directly publishes the corrected nominal 774M size, superseding the paper's erroneous 762M label.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review of the original card, implementation and report, plus targeted later active/activated-parameter searches for GPT-2 large, 774M, 762M and 0.774B, found no supported active-count convention for the complete original checkpoint. Chang and Bergen measure sparse masked subnetworks; Marek et al. report a structurally modified GPT-2 small training experiment. Neither transfers to the released large model. Dense architecture alone does not establish total-equals-active.

architecture.note: A dense decoder-only Transformer with 36 blocks, hidden width 1,280, 20 attention heads and 5,120-wide feed-forward layers; no expert routing.

context_window.note: Exact configuration, learned position table and technical report agree on 1,024 tokens.

modalities.note: The released model consumes tokenized text and produces text-token logits for generation; no additional modality modules are present.

reasoning.note: Commonsense reasoning evaluations do not specify a dedicated reasoning mode. Absence of a feature specification is not a tested inability.

tool_call.note: The original interface specifies text generation, with no documented structured tool-calling protocol. Retain unknown instead of claiming categorical inability.

description.value: Large GPT-2 checkpoint, a 36-layer dense Transformer trained on WebText for autoregressive text generation.
description.note: Replace generic staged-release wording with the documented architecture, training corpus and generation function.

Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

patch.notes: Publicly released on August 20, 2019 after earlier selected-partner sharing. The original configuration and implementation support exactly 774,030,080 learned parameters, counting tied token embeddings once; 774M is OpenAI's corrected nominal label, replacing 762M. Active parameters are not separately established for this checkpoint. The release originally carried MIT; the current official repository publishes Modified MIT terms introduced in January 2020.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the precise 774,030,080 total after fresh original configuration/code corroboration and confirms OpenAI's corrected nominal 774M specification. Active parameters remain undisclosed: targeted later research yields sparse-subnetwork counts or modified GPT-2 small experiments, not a convention for the complete original large checkpoint. The other 12 field assessments are preserved.
